acceptanceCriteria: An explicit opt-in export records exact request/options, Git commit/tree/blob identities, engine/profile identity, bounded necessary inputs and the original receipt; read commands never create a bundle implicitly.

A second checkout can reproduce the admitted read-only context/proof result from the frozen inputs, or returns precise missing-input/unsupported-version reasons. Verification compares meaningful result fields with any nondeterministic exclusions specified in advance.

Replayed or mocked outputs are visibly historical or synthetic and cannot satisfy a fresh verification, authority, promotion or learning claim. Drift, tampering, missing Git objects, mixed worktrees and incompatible engines have explicit outcomes.
Export is local, bounded and secret-screened; inspection precedes any sharing. No credentials, arbitrary command auto-execution, network fetch, hidden daemon or implicit learning is introduced.

Retain a real failure reproduction on a second checkout and focused hostile-input tests; bind source/tool versions and acceptance evidence, define rollback and preserve all existing checkpoint and frozen wire gates.
body: Owner requested all five n8n-inspired improvements as part of Corvint 0.7.0 on 2026-09-22. Original Go implementations of the patterns; no n8n source import. Extend the cited existing mechanisms. This ticket records release intent, not delivery or promotion. Before implementation is called complete, update the owning indexed spec with stable requirements, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence and rollback, and finish normal CEM/OCM, independent review and mandatory gates. Extend docs/specs/falsifiable-packet-v0.md and cmd/corvint/prove_checkpoint.go; checkpoint revalidation exists but is not full execution replay. Prior art: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/blob/main/docs/build/understand-workflows/understand-executions/debug-executions.md and docs/build/work-with-data/pin-and-mock-data.md in that repository.
title: Export bounded local bundles that reproduce context failures
